{'text': "A new report from Counterpoint Research shows that Apple surpassed Samsung in Q2 2026 to become the top-selling smartphone brand in European carrier channels, as carrier performance outpaced the overall market. Here's the full breakdown."}

{'text': 'Apple drives carrier sales, outperforming the wider European smartphone market'}

{'text': 'In a report published today, Counterpoint Research noted that smartphone sales through European carriers declined 4% year-over-year in Q2 2026, compared with an 11% drop in the open market. Overall smartphone sales fell 8%, according to the report.'}

{'text': "Counterpoint said the results once again reflect the impact of rising memory costs, with Europe's low-end smartphone market hit particularly hard. Carrier channels fared relatively better because sales through that channel tend to skew toward higher-end models and premium brands, including Apple, and because more consumers are choosing to purchase handsets on contract."}

{'text': "The report noted that Apple's share of European carrier smartphone sales rose from 33% in Q2 2025 to 37% in Q2 2026, while Samsung's share fell from 39% to 34% over the same period."}

{'text': 'However, in terms of year-over-year growth, Chinese brand vivo was the standout performer, with carrier sales up 90%; Motorola trailed far behind with a 27% increase.'}

{'text': "Here's what Counterpoint Research Associate Director Jan Stryjak had to say about the numbers:"}

{'text': 'Stryjak added that he expects carrier channels to continue gaining market share over the "next few quarters," as the "memory crisis" continues to weigh on the low-end market. He also noted that independent retailers are running more aggressive promotions than carriers, which "could help offset some of the pricing pressure and provide an additional boost to the open market."'}
